Subject: Issue: can't accept portal invite (SSO multihop)

Hi Mateo,

We received the supplier portal invite yesterday but when our users click Accept they land on a blank page and the CTA never renders. We tested both Chrome and Edge. Our Identity team says the assertion is being proxied through an internal hub and RelayState looks like it does a second redirect.

Attached is a screenshot of what the user sees and our SSO team captured a short trace. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports an extra redirect in the SAML flow? We can try to provide additional logs.

Thanks,

Hi Ellen — thanks for the details and the trace. Sorry you're hitting this.

Quick overview of what I'll check from our side:
- Whether the portal's Accept CTA is stripped when RelayState contains an extra path fragment.
- If our session cookie is set before the second redirect completes (multihop race).
- Whether the portal render path uses referer/origin checks that could reject the final frame.

Ben, can you pull the request/response logs for the invite token "xyz" and check for Set-Cookie ordering vs 302 redirects? Monica — please pull the tenant's model (SupplyLogic Inc.) SAML config to confirm the AssertionConsumerService URL list.

Ellen — would you be able to test accepting in an incognito window and, if available, capture the browser network waterfall? That helps us quickly determine if a cookie is missing vs markup failing.

I'll follow up with an investigation summary by 2pm PT.

— Mateo

Subject: Re: Issue: can't accept portal invite (SSO multihop)

Thanks — dug in and reproduced locally using a test relay. Notes: 
- When the initial /sso/consume sets session cookie after the first POST, our runtime sometimes emits Set-Cookie in the second redirect response instead of the final 200. Browsers drop Set-Cookie on cross-site 302 in some cases (depends on SameSite and Secure flags).
- The Accept CTA is rendered client-side after a short script that checks for the session cookie; if the cookie isn't present the DOM leaves the CTA out (we show a blank placeholder).

Action plan (short):
1) Temporary workaround: instruct SupplyLogic users to open Accept in incognito or disable any iframe blockers (this forces a fresh cookie store).
2) Medium fix (hours): change our accept flow to set the cookie on the final 200 response body via a small JS write if missing (backstop for 302-drop).
3) Long term (next sprint): route SAML relay handoffs through our session proxy to guarantee Set-Cookie ordering across multihop proxies.

I've attached the trimmed server trace we captured while reproducing. It includes the Set-Cookie timing.

Attachments: sso-trace-20261105.txt (text/plain)
